title: Non-Refundable Security Deposit
plainEnglish: Your security deposit will not be returned under any circumstances.
counterClause: Security deposit shall be returned within 30 days of vacating, minus documented deductions.
negotiationTip: Request an itemised list of all conditions that could lead to deductions before signing.

title: Excessive Deposit Deductions
plainEnglish: The landlord can deduct large amounts from your deposit for minor wear and tear.
counterClause: Deductions are limited to damage beyond normal wear and tear, with receipts provided.
negotiationTip: Take timestamped photos of the property on move-in day as evidence.

title: Lock-In Period
plainEnglish: You cannot leave before the lock-in period ends without paying a penalty.
counterClause: A break clause shall be available after 3 months with 30 days written notice.
negotiationTip: Always negotiate a break clause, especially for leases longer than 6 months.

title: Early Exit Penalty
plainEnglish: Leaving before the lease ends will cost you a significant financial penalty.
counterClause: Early termination penalty shall not exceed one month's rent.
negotiationTip: Cap the penalty to one month's rent and get it written into the contract.

title: Unilateral Rent Increase
plainEnglish: The landlord can raise your rent at any time without your agreement.
counterClause: Rent may only be increased once per year with 60 days written notice and by no more than the CPI rate.
negotiationTip: Negotiate a fixed rent for the full lease term, or cap annual increases.

title: Short Notice Period
plainEnglish: You could be asked to leave with very little advance warning.
counterClause: Landlord must provide a minimum of 60 days written notice to vacate.
negotiationTip: Ensure the notice period for both parties is equal and at least 30 days.

title: Tenant Responsible for All Repairs
plainEnglish: You may have to pay for repairs that are normally the landlord's responsibility.
counterClause: Structural and appliance repairs are the landlord's responsibility. Tenant is responsible for minor maintenance only.
negotiationTip: Define a clear threshold — e.g. repairs under $50 are your responsibility, above that is landlord's.

title: Hidden Utility Charges
plainEnglish: Costs beyond rent — like utilities and service fees — may not be clearly disclosed upfront.
counterClause: All charges beyond the monthly rent shall be itemised and agreed upon before signing.
negotiationTip: Ask for an estimate of average monthly utility costs before committing.

title: Landlord Entry Without Notice
plainEnglish: The landlord can enter your home without giving you advance notice.
counterClause: Landlord must provide at least 24 hours written notice before entering the property.
negotiationTip: This is a legal right in most jurisdictions — check local tenancy law.

title: Eviction Without Court Order
plainEnglish: The landlord may attempt to remove you without going through a formal legal eviction process.
counterClause: Any eviction must follow due legal process as required by applicable tenancy law.
negotiationTip: Self-help evictions are illegal in most jurisdictions — document everything.

title: No Subletting Allowed
plainEnglish: You are not allowed to rent out a room or the property to anyone else.
counterClause: Tenant may sublet with landlord's written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
negotiationTip: If you may need to sublet, negotiate this right upfront.

title: Automatic Lease Renewal
plainEnglish: Your lease will automatically renew unless you give notice within a specific window.
counterClause: Lease renewal requires written agreement from both parties at least 30 days before expiry.
negotiationTip: Set a calendar reminder well before the notice deadline.

title: Holdover Rent Penalty
plainEnglish: Staying past the lease end date can result in double or triple rent charges.
counterClause: Holdover tenancy shall continue at the existing rent rate on a month-to-month basis.
negotiationTip: Clarify the exact holdover terms before signing.

title: Tenant Liable for Landlord Legal Costs
plainEnglish: If any dispute goes to court, you may be required to pay the landlord's legal fees.
counterClause: Each party shall bear their own legal costs in the event of a dispute.
negotiationTip: This clause is one-sided — request that it either be removed or made mutual.

title: Waiver of Right to Sue
plainEnglish: You give up the right to take the landlord to court for disputes.
counterClause: Both parties retain the right to pursue legal remedies in a court of competent jurisdiction.
negotiationTip: Never waive your right to go to court — this is a serious red flag.

title: No Alteration Clause
plainEnglish: You cannot make any changes to the property, including painting, without written approval.
counterClause: Tenant may make minor cosmetic changes that can be reversed upon vacating.
negotiationTip: Negotiate the right to make small reversible changes like hanging pictures.

title: Pet Prohibition
plainEnglish: Keeping pets is not allowed or requires written landlord approval.
counterClause: Tenant may keep one pet with prior written consent, subject to an additional refundable deposit.
negotiationTip: Negotiate a pet addendum if you have or plan to get a pet.

title: No Rent Receipt Obligation
plainEnglish: The landlord is not required to provide proof of your rent payments.
counterClause: Landlord shall provide a written receipt for every payment received within 3 business days.
negotiationTip: Always pay by bank transfer so you have automatic proof of payment.

title: Responsibility for Common Areas
plainEnglish: You may be held responsible for the upkeep of shared spaces.
counterClause: Maintenance of common areas is the landlord's responsibility.
negotiationTip: Clarify who is responsible for cleaning and repairs in shared spaces.

title: Parking Fee Not Included
plainEnglish: Parking is not included in the rent and will be charged as an additional cost.
counterClause: One parking space is included in the monthly rent at no additional charge.
negotiationTip: Get the total cost including parking in writing before signing.

title: Guest Restrictions
plainEnglish: Having guests stay overnight may require landlord approval.
counterClause: Tenant may have guests stay for up to 14 consecutive days without landlord approval.
negotiationTip: Clarify the guest policy if you expect family or friends to visit.

title: Force Majeure — Landlord Not Liable
plainEnglish: The landlord is not responsible if the property becomes uninhabitable due to events outside their control.
counterClause: If the property becomes uninhabitable for any reason, rent obligations shall be suspended.
negotiationTip: Ensure the clause covers your right to terminate if the property becomes uninhabitable.

title: Noise and Conduct Restrictions
plainEnglish: There are strict rules about noise levels and behaviour that could lead to eviction if broken.
counterClause: Conduct rules must be reasonable, clearly defined, and applied equally to all tenants.
negotiationTip: Ask for a copy of the full house rules before signing.

title: Governing Law
plainEnglish: Disputes must be resolved under a specific jurisdiction's law.
counterClause: This agreement shall be governed by the laws of the jurisdiction where the property is located.
negotiationTip: Ensure the governing law matches where the property actually is.

title: Entire Agreement Clause
plainEnglish: Only the written contract counts. Verbal promises by the landlord are not enforceable.
counterClause: All representations made during the letting process must be documented in this agreement.
negotiationTip: Get every landlord promise in writing before you sign.
